overview: This 516-page file traces Japan’s wartime and postwar food shortages through production studies, rationing laws, SCAP reports, and U.S. and Allied debates over grain imports. It follows emergency crop collections, competition for scarce global supplies, nutritional conditions, and disputes over foreign residents’ rations from 1945 to 1949.
interest: Detailed statistics, Japanese food-control laws, and internal policy disputes reveal how occupation authorities balanced famine prevention against global shortages.
